subject: Urgent: ACME Corp live stream degradation — client SDK streaming parser suspected
messages:
From: Sam Wu <sam.wu@acmecorp.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Live ingestion latency and error spike — urgent

Irene / Monica,

We started seeing a sharp regression on our production streaming ingest at ~08:47 PST. Symptoms: 95th p99 latency jumped from ~120ms to ~2.3s, overall throughput dropped ~35%, and error rate increased to ~5% (5xx from Redwood). The impact is visible in our checkout pipeline and on customer-facing features.

We attached an SDK trace (sdk-trace-headers.pcap) and a short log dump (acme-logs-20261118.txt). The traces show bursts of connector-level retransmits and repeated re-negotiation of the stream. This looks different than prior transient load spikes — the failures correlate with requests that include long metadata headers.

Can you triage? This is blocking several customers; our Ops team has paused non-critical processing. Happy to hop on a call.

Thanks,
Sam Wu
VP Engineering, ACME Corp
Attachments: acme-logs-20261118.txt, sdk-trace-headers.pcap

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 10:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Live ingestion latency and error spike — initial triage notes

Team —

Quick first-pass after loading the pcap: there are repeated occurrences of partial header frames where the client appears to split long metadata headers across multiple TCP frames. Our SDK streaming parser performs an incremental header reassembly pass that, on some older client versions (v2.3.1 and earlier), mishandles header continuations when a frame boundary arrives mid-header token. When that happens we see a small window where the stream state is ambiguous and the runtime falls back to a synchronous reparse, causing backpressure spikes and dropped tokens.

What I observed:
- Repeated "header-continuation" sequences from the client with header lines > 512 bytes.
- Runtime logs show parse retries and a surge of sync re-parses (these line up with p99 latencies in the trace).
- No obvious memory corruption, but the parser's state machine isn't recognizing continuation markers reliably for a subset of header encodings.

Immediate recommendations:
1) Can ACME confirm SDK version and whether they have "enable_multi_frame_headers" enabled?
2) As a short-term mitigation, we can flip edge gateway to coalesce incoming frames (coalesce_window=25ms) to avoid boundary splits. This trades a little tail latency for correctness until we ship a patch.
3) I'll prepare a small reproducer and a unit-test for header-continuation cases; target time to a patch candidate is 48 hours.

Assigning: karthik -> root cause & patch; marissa -> canary plan; monica -> customer comms + ops window.

Karthik Iyer
Staff Software Engineer, Runtime
Redwood Inference
Attachments: snippet: parser-stack.log (excerpt)

Sam —

Thanks for the rapid report. Two immediate items that will help us triage and reduce customer impact:

1) Please enable SDK debug logging on one of the affected nodes and share the next pcap capture. In particular we need the client-side SDK version and the full header payloads for failing streams.
2) Would ACME be able to accept a short maintenance window today from 16:00-17:00 PST for us to temporarily enable frame coalescing at the edge and monitor the effect? We expect this to reduce the mis-split header cases quickly.

I've attached a quick SLO snapshot to illustrate the regression. If the maintenance window works, we'll coordinate steps and hold a 15-minute post-check call.

Monica Patel

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Live ingestion latency and error spike — action plan and owners

All —

Summary and next steps after the investigation this afternoon:

Root cause (suspected): intermittent client SDK header fragmentation combined with an edge-case in our streaming parser's continuation handling on older SDK builds. This causes synchronous re-parses under load which drive p99 latency spikes and token drops.

Immediate plan:
- Short-term mitigation (today): enable edge coalescing (coalesce_window=25ms) at the customer's ingress to reduce frame splits; monitor for 1 hour. Owner: Marissa Cole.
- Patch (48 hours): engineering will produce a parser fix that correctly recognizes header continuation markers and adds a defensive check for truncated tokens. Owner: Karthik Iyer.
- Rollout (post-patch): staged canary in Dedicated, then widen to Hosted for affected regions. Owner: Marissa Cole.
- Customer comms & verification: Monica will coordinate the ops window and collect SDK debug captures; once we have the patch candidate we'll schedule a joint validation with ACME. Owner: Monica Patel.

Consequence management: If the patch candidate regresses, we will revert to the coalescing mitigation and open an incident rollback playbook.

Links and artifacts: JIRA-INFRA-3492, https://drive.google.com/file/d/1AcmeTraceShare, attached logs and pcap.

I'll join the 3pm PST bridge with ACME to walk through the plan.

Irene Choi
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
Attachments: acme-logs-20261118.txt, sdk-trace-headers.pcap, slo-latency-chart.png
